_README: CENSUS OF EVERY OBSERVER IN THIS REPO THAT DECIDES WHETHER SOMETHING ELSE IS ALIVE.
Enforced by tests/test_observer_contract.py. You do not opt in to this file and you
cannot forget it: the harness DISCOVERS its own subjects from the source tree by two
structural rules and fails on anything it finds that is not listed here.
Rule A (risk)     — a file under scripts/ or dashboard/ that identifies a process by
name/argv (pgrep, pidof, ps -e, ps aux) must appear below.
Rule B (adoption) — a file that sources observer_guard.sh must appear below with
contract 'v1', which subjects it to the behavioural battery.
contract values:
v1        — adopted. Exposes `<script> observe` printing state=present|absent|
unobservable and exiting 0|1|3. The harness runs the full battery
against it, including that it SUPPRESSES corrective action while blind
and still ACTS when the target is genuinely absent.
unadopted — a known instance of the defect class, not yet migrated. MUST name an
owning handoff and a task marker; the harness verifies an UNCHECKED
'- [ ]' line carrying that marker really exists in that file. A deferral
that is checked off or deleted without the migration turns this suite
RED. Deferring is allowed; deferring silently is not.
exempt    — reviewed and out of scope, with the reason recorded. Reviewed, not
forgotten: the row is the review.
Origin: 2026-08-12. bus_supervisor.sh identified the coordinator-daemon with
`pgrep -f 'session_bus_coordinator\.py run'`; the live daemon's argv had
'--bus-root <path>' between '.py' and 'run'. The pattern matched nothing, the
watchdog declared a healthy heartbeating daemon dead FOREVER, and relaunch-looped
for hours with nobody watching. Two signals were available and it required BOTH, so
the working one was overruled by the broken one and 'cannot tell' became 'dead'.

_roots_note: artifacts/operator/ is deliberately OUT of discovery scope: those are one-shot
ratifiers a human runs and reads once, not long-running observers whose verdict
nobody sees. Two of them do gate on an argv pattern and are recorded below as
'exempt' rows with the reason, so the finding is not lost — but a new ratifier
must not turn this suite red on an unrelated commit. A guard that forbids its own
neighbours' idiom gets deleted by the first person it blocks.
_self_exclude_note: The contract library itself. It matches Rule A only because its header QUOTES the
specimen's `pgrep -f` line while explaining why that shape is forbidden. Excluding it
by data, not by a special case in the test — and only this one file, so a second
'explanatory' mention elsewhere still trips the rule.
_adoption_pattern_note: An actual `source` statement, not any MENTION of the file. Matching a bare
mention flagged this contract's own census module for quoting the library's path
in its docstring — a guard tripping on prose about itself. Rule A stays a plain
mention match on purpose: writing `pgrep` in a scripts/ file is worth a moment's
thought even in a comment, and the one file that discusses it at length is listed

observers.notes: Reference adoption. Was the exact twin of the specimen: `runner_pids() { pgrep -f "$RUNNER_PATTERN"; }` + `[[ -n "$(runner_pids)" ]] && (( age <= STALE_AFTER ))`, and it kill -9'd every pid the pattern returned, on a shared host, on a boolean that could not distinguish dead from unseen. Its runner already published its own pid in heartbeat.json and the supervisor did not read it.

THE SPECIMEN. Being repaired in a parallel session (C49) as this row is written — the repair replaces the pattern with the heartbeat pid, which removes the instance. This row keeps the FILE enrolled so the class stays enforced afterwards: adopting observer_guard.sh + an `observe` entrypoint is what subjects it to the battery. Not edited from here; the file has a live owner.

Identity is correctly port-based (it already migrated off `pgrep -f 'dashboard\.server .*--port 8100'`) and hub_source_is_newer() is a model three-valued predicate returning a distinct 2 for every unknown. But health_ok() is two-valued: a curl timeout, a removed curl binary, a hub moved off :8100 and a genuinely dead hub are one value, and cmd_loop restarts on it. Separately, check_hub_stale_source is called only from cmd_once and never from cmd_loop — the C42 bug the bus supervisor already fixed — while the header claims the running supervisor now notices a stale hub. Not edited from here: the hub supervisor is a long-running script and editing a running .sh is its own incident class.

`pgrep -f 'llama-server|llama.cpp' | xargs ... || true` summed into an RSS total. Every failure mode — pgrep missing, argv drift, a renamed binary, an xargs error — yields 0 GB, which takes the else branch and prints 'No heavy inference detected'. FAIL-OPEN: run_wrapper.sh then launches the full multi-project agent workload on top of a live 200GB+ inference run. Two states where three are needed, in the dangerous direction.

`autopilot_running() { pgrep -f 'scripts/autopilot/autopilot.py start'; }` requires `start` to sit immediately after the script path — the specimen's failure, verbatim. Any `autopilot.py --config X start` reads as 'AutoPilot not running' and the lab shadow jobs launch into a live AutoPilot.

Partly right already: a pgrep returncode outside (0,1) is treated as 'could not inspect'. But an empty result is read as a positive 'no AutoPilot' and green-lights a bench against a live one, and a MISSING pgrep binary raises FileNotFoundError out of run() before reaching that handling.

`pgrep -f "claude"` is a bare substring matching any argv containing 'claude', including its own caller. `pgrep -f "monitor_storage"` makes a renamed/relocated monitor read as permanently absent, so the check permanently recommends starting a second one. Several probes use `|| echo unknown` and then COMPARE 'unknown' against the expected value, reporting FAIL — an unreadable /sys node in a container is scored as a misconfiguration. Report-only, but it gates session start.

`sudo pkill -f claude` on a documented shared host — the exact idiom CLAUDE.md and INC-20260731-broad-process-pattern-kills forbid, committed in-repo. The PreToolUse pattern-kill hook cannot see it: the hook inspects the typed command (`bash scripts/session/emergency_cleanup.sh`), not the script body, so the rule is assumed-enforced here rather than enforced. Interactive prompt is the only thing between it and every other session's processes.

observers.reason: REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION, not a gap. _pgrep returns None for 'tool unavailable' and every consumer routes that to unconfirmed/pgrep_missing; mi210_state fails closed to device_state 'unknown'; is_quiet_window names each unconfirmable signal in its reason list. It states the polarity rule this whole contract encodes: 'for EXCLUSION, unknown must mean busy; for ACCUSATION, unknown must mean silence.' Residual (argv drift reads as a positive 'none' rather than unconfirmed) is recorded under OBS-5's neighbourhood, not enforced here.

REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION. daemon_liveness returns True|False|None, handles PermissionError as alive-under-another-uid, and returns True-with-the-doubt-stated when identity is unverifiable; heartbeat_freshness keeps liveness and freshness on separate axes. This is the standard the rest of the repo is being held to.
